A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GEB research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including distinguishing relocated material from actual additions and removals.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM alignment evaluations, ablations, repeated-run results and a synthetic bandit experiment in Section 5 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v4 retains original alignment and bandit results and adds a hard-prompt math reasoning experiment, revised repeated-run summaries and significance tests.

M1.justification: The GEB objective in Equations 8–11, three bonus instantiations in Table 2, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. Restricting bonuses to rejected responses was already documented in v3. The new math experiment applies the existing method.

E1.justification: v4 adds math preference training on DAPO-MATH-17K prompts selected for low initial correct-answer likelihood, plus OlympiadBench and AIME 2025 evaluation. MATH500, previously used for evaluating alignment-trained models, also appears in this new reasoning setting. Existing alignment and bandit coverage remains.

E2.justification: FEB disappears from the repeated in-domain comparison, changing v3 Table 8 to v4 Table 7, although it remains in main Tables 3–4. The main comparator membership, including f-DPO, SELM, XPO and VPO, is unchanged. The new math comparison uses the already represented DPO baseline.

E3.justification: v4 introduces a separate Qwen2.5-7B reasoning protocol: remove prompts solved within two samples at temperature 0.6, retain 12K prompts, construct verifier-labeled correct/incorrect preference pairs, train under KL divergence, and evaluate Pass@16. These are settings for an added experiment; the original alignment and bandit protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 adds a targeted real-math stress test of whether GEB helps when correct answers are initially difficult to sample. The existing bonus-strength sensitivity, rejected-response ablation, semantic-coherence analysis, sampling-distribution analysis and toy bandit experiment are retained, with some relocated.

E5.justification: Statistical validation changes from three runs with means and standard deviations in v3 Appendix F.1 to five runs in v4 Appendix E.1. v4 also adds systematic significance-test p-values against f-DPO across both backbones and three divergences in Table 8. The precise test family is not specified beyond 'independent p-test.'

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports DPO/GEB-1/π Pass@16 of 89.80/93.00 on MATH500, 57.78/65.78 on OlympiadBench and 23.23/29.48 on AIME 2025 under the new reasoning setting. Three-run summaries are replaced by five-run summaries, FEB entries disappear from that comparison, and p-values are added. Main Tables 3–5 and the relocated ablation/coherence results retain their values.

T1.justification: v4 removes v3's entire Appendix C, 'Regret Bound,' including Assumptions C.1–C.2, the preference generalized eluder coefficient definition, Theorem C.1 and its derivation in Equations 25–40. The core failure and optimism definitions, results and proofs in Sections 3–4 and Appendix B remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: prior theoretical bonus formulations fail optimism, GEB satisfies the proposed condition and encompasses heuristic bonuses, and experiments support alignment improvements across divergences and backbones.

C2.justification: The explanation that GEB helps when preferred responses have low reference probability already appears in v3's toy study and is applied to v4's math results. Interpretations concerning bonus strength, curvature of u, rejected responses and semantic coherence are retained. No substantive new limitation is stated.

D1.justification: v4 documents the new math experiment's filtering and verification procedure, learning rate, warm-up ratio and bonus coefficients. Existing implementation and hardware details move from Appendix D.1 to C.1 unchanged. The public GitHub link already existed; checklist removal eliminates its additional anonymous code links.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to the Qwen2.5 technical report and DAPO, and removes Zhong et al.'s GEC reference alongside the regret analysis. Appendix A's research positioning is otherwise retained. Citation-style changes and shortened author lists do not represent new related work.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v4 adds acknowledgment, reproducibility and ethics statements, removes the NeurIPS checklist, and relocates semantic-coherence and rejected-response discussions to the appendix. Headings and citation formatting change with the conference template.

P2.justification: v4 adopts ICLR typography and headers, adds the math-results and p-value tables, and relocates existing displays. v3 Tables 6–7 become appendix Tables 10 and 9, respectively, while the repeated-run table loses FEB rows. Existing figures retain their plotted content and visual designs.

improvement.justification: The hard-prompt math study tests a practical condition under which GEB is intended to help, while five-run summaries and explicit p-values make empirical reliability easier to assess. These gains are tempered by removal of the regret analysis and repeated FEB comparison. The core optimism proofs remain, and the removed regret bound already scaled linearly with T, supporting a limited net improvement.
